description: body-write-after-freeze with what the port still refuses through the body after a freeze put in (D24 item 3). Through the transaction's body, or another cursor at its slot, a path whose first part is a write, a plain write and write_if_empty go on after a db_freeze or a concat, as a path that begins with an init does. Still refused with StaleCursor, before anything is written: a byte writer through the body, a path through it whose first part is neither an init nor a write, an empty path, and a write first, a plain write or write_if_empty through any other cursor from before the freeze, what a concat gives back and the cursor it was called on included. Nothing refused writes anything, so nothing is poisoned and each transaction commits. What the port writes is what Zig writes with the refused ops left out, which is body-write-after-freeze.
